case.pattern_description: The pattern involves a single Android device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) that was used to make online purchases of product C on multiple customers' cards, including card C07472-K1, with all transactions marked as New and routed through an anonymous proxy. It affects debit-card holders in billing region 315, as the device appeared on 28 different cards (52 cards total) within 19 days and was linked to four previously confirmed fraud cases. The activity was discovered through a monitor sweep that flagged the device profile shared across several cards, prompting an analyst review and resulting in a fraud verdict.

case.summary: The alert was triggered by a monitor sweep that identified the device profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080 being used on 28 cards in November and December, all behind an anonymous proxy. The strongest fraud indicators are that this device profile has been seen on only 52 cards ever but made 60 purchases on 28 different customers' cards within 19 days, appears in four confirmed-fraud cases and is labelled undocumented, while the model risk score of 0.10 for the flagged transaction translates to a calibrated fraud rate of 3 % for product C in the same score band. The case is judged to be fraud with a probability of 95 %. The recommended actions are to block the card, open a new case, file a report, monitor the connected cards and escalate the matter to an analyst.

sar.narrative: The cardholder identified as customer C07472, holder of visa debit card C07472-K1, was the subject of two unauthorized online purchases using product code C in billing region 315. The first transaction, id 3500431 for $56.19, occurred on 2016-11-30 at 15:47, and the second, flagged transaction id 3512563 for $209.66, occurred on 2016-12-04 at 11:47. Both purchases were executed from the same device profile "SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080" and originated through the online channel. Analysis shows that this device profile has been observed on only 52 cards, yet it was used for 60 purchases on 28 different customers' cards within 19 days, all marked New and routed through an anonymous proxy. The device also appears in four previously closed confirmed-fraud cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035) and is linked to 27 other cards, including C01289-K1, C01996-K2, C02910-K1, C02975-K1, C03676-K2, C04108-K2, C04274-K1, and C05448-K2. The pattern of activity matches none of the documented fraud typologies and is classified as an undocumented device-ring scheme. Because the transactions were made by an unauthorized party, the activity is deemed suspicious and warranted immediate containment actions, including blocking the card and monitoring connected cards. The cardholder has not yet been contacted.
